label: Fredholm Theory
notes: Appendix A is the functional-analytic control room behind smooth moduli spaces. Across printed pages 531 to 548 we learn how an infinite-dimensional nonlinear equation collapses into a finite-dimensional, orientable, generically regular local model, governed by one integer: the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy-Riemann operator.

label: Fredholm Operators
notes: A bounded operator between Banach spaces is Fredholm when its kernel is finite-dimensional, its range is closed, and its cokernel is finite-dimensional. These three conditions isolate exactly the finite data we can count, while the bulk of the infinite-dimensional map remains an isomorphism between complementary subspaces.

label: The Fredholm Index
notes: The index subtracts cokernel dimension from kernel dimension, producing the dimension budget every later moduli computation spends. Although kernel and cokernel can each jump under deformation, their difference is a discrete invariant. This integer, not the individual defect spaces, is what the appendix protects and propagates.

label: Stability of the Index
notes: The index is locally constant in the operator norm, so it cannot change under a small continuous deformation. Equivalently, Fredholm operators form an open set on which the index is a continuous, hence constant, integer along any path connecting two operators within the same component.

label: Compact Perturbations
notes: Adding any compact operator leaves the index unchanged: kernel and cokernel may both move, but their difference is pinned. This is why the linearized Cauchy-Riemann operator, which differs from a model operator by compact lower-order terms, inherits a computable index from the model.

label: Determinant Lines
notes: The determinant line tensors the top exterior power of the kernel with that of the cokernel, packaging both orientations into a single real line. Along an index-zero path with invertible endpoints the line can still twist; the parity of regular kernel crossings records whether orientation is preserved or reversed.

label: Implicit Function Theorem
notes: When the linearization is onto with a bounded right inverse, the implicit function theorem in Banach spaces graphs the zero set over the kernel. The nonlinear equation is corrected along the image of the right inverse while the free directions live in the kernel, exactly as in the planar model shown.

label: Regular Values and Submersions
notes: A value is regular when the derivative is surjective with complemented kernel at every preimage. The Banach implicit function theorem then makes the preimage a smooth submanifold whose tangent space is the kernel of the linearization, giving its dimension as the Fredholm index of that operator.

label: Kuranishi Reduction
notes: At a singular point the derivative may fail to be onto, so a pseudoinverse splits the equation into image equations, solved by the implicit function theorem, and a finite obstruction map valued in the cokernel. The local zero set becomes the zero set of this finite obstruction over the kernel.

label: Sard-Smale
notes: Sard-Smale upgrades finite-dimensional Sard to Fredholm maps between separable Banach spaces: regular values form a residual set. The proof splits domain and target along kernel and cokernel complements, reducing regularity at each fiber to ordinary Sard in finitely many variables, then patches using separability.

label: Smooth Moduli Spaces
notes: Applied to the universal moduli problem, these tools make the space of J-holomorphic curves a smooth manifold for generic almost complex structures. Its dimension equals the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy-Riemann operator, the single integer that this entire appendix has been engineered to compute and protect.

label: Recap and Pipeline
notes: To summarize: finiteness plus closed range defines Fredholm; the index is the stable difference of defects; stability under small and compact perturbations makes it computable; implicit-function, Kuranishi, and Sard-Smale convert that index into a smooth, oriented, correctly dimensioned moduli manifold for generic data.
